item.title: How Trump’s ‘One Big Beautiful Bill’ Could Change How You File Taxes This Year
item.description: Many filers will be able to claim bigger deductions this year, thanks to new rules in the tax code. We spoke to the experts to learn who's eligible for these credits and how to claim them.

item.title: How an Aging California Is Turning to Senior Centers for Romance, Community and Health
item.description: No two senior centers are alike. We visited three very different venues in L.A. to learn how they’re changing for California’s aging population.

item.title: The Pay Phone That Lets San Franciscans ‘Call a Republican’
item.description: Two pay phones, in San Francisco and Abilene, Texas, aimed to connect Americans across political divides.

item.title: Ciao Bella: Do Italians Still Live in San Francisco’s North Beach?
item.description: San Francisco’s North Beach neighborhood is known for its Italian restaurants, cafes and bakeries. But is it still an enclave for Northern California’s Italian immigrants?

item.title: Widespread Kaiser Strike to End After 4 Weeks With No Deal Yet
item.description: The large, open-ended strike had led to frustrations by some patients over delayed care as well as difficulties for workers who went weeks without a paycheck.

item.title: West Oakland RV Fire Cause of Hourslong BART Transbay Tube Shutdown
item.description: The fire created a communications failure that shut down service between Oakland and San Francisco for nearly 12 hours.

item.title: Oakland Teachers Approve a Strike, as Report Calls District’s Pay ‘Not Competitive’
item.description: The Oakland Unified School District’s teachers union voted to authorize a strike after nearly a year of unsuccessful contract talks, but said it doesn’t plan to walk out imminently.

item.description: City leaders have called for a public utility option for years, but have struggled to push through the California utility giant’s lobbying efforts and legal challenges.
